mission: PBUF FND-004 Consequences of the Three-Dimensional Microscopic Ontology

axioms.A1: Spacetime has three independent microscopic degrees of freedom corresponding to the three spatial dimensions.
axioms.A2: Matter couples identically to each microscopic degree through g_dev=1/137.
axioms.A3: Macroscopic continuum behaviour emerges by coarse graining the microscopic state.

auxiliary_conditions.C1: q transforms as the defining spatial-vector representation and no background direction is present.
auxiliary_conditions.C2: The long-wave theory is local, analytic, homogeneous, parity-even and rotationally invariant.
auxiliary_conditions.C3: The reference state is stable and nondegenerate, and retained modes separate from microscopic scales.
auxiliary_conditions.C4: A covariant scalarization/source map is specified and non-observed modes decouple.
auxiliary_conditions.C5: Time dynamics (inertial or dissipative) and kinetic normalization are specified.
auxiliary_conditions.C6: Light couples to a specified effective metric or ray-deflection functional.
auxiliary_conditions.C7: The matter-coupling normalization is fixed independently of all other source coefficients.

consequences.prediction: Exactly three microscopic component labels; generic N has N and a scalar has one.
consequences.observable: Component count is physical only if components can be independently excited/read out.
No component-dependent coupling at the axiom scale.

consequences.prediction: The equal-coupling vector is the normalized singlet direction and two source-orthogonal combinations are unsourced by a common scalar load.
consequences.observable: Two dark combinations exist at linear source level, but their propagation is not fixed.

consequences.prediction: The coherent source strength carries a sqrt(3) amplitude (factor 3 in a quadratic response) relative to one equally normalized component.
consequences.conditions: independent orthonormal components; linear response; same per-component susceptibility
consequences.observable: N ontology replaces 3 by N; scalar has factor 1.

consequences.prediction: A rotationally invariant rank-two constitutive tensor in the vector sector has transverse/longitudinal form.
consequences.observable: One longitudinal and two degenerate transverse eigenmodes.

consequences.prediction: The leading static vector continuum equation has two gradient stiffnesses, not a uniquely fixed scalar Helmholtz law.
consequences.observable: G_T=a and G_L=a+b; positivity requires K>0, a>0, a+b>0.

consequences.prediction: If only the common/longitudinal scalar sector is retained, the CORE-type scalar equation follows in form.
consequences.observable: The axioms fix neither K, G nor s(rho); the equation is not inevitable from A1-A3 alone.

consequences.prediction: Isotropy forbids component-dependent masses and directional stiffness at leading order.
consequences.observable: Splitting signals broken isotropy, unequal coupling, or extra structure.

consequences.prediction: Propagation has one longitudinal and two transverse branches when inertial vector dynamics is supplied.
consequences.observable: Three fixes transverse degeneracy at two; N internal components generally gives N-1 source-orthogonal modes, not spatial L/T modes unless it is a vector.

consequences.prediction: g_dev directly fixes the normalized common matter vertex, but A2 postulates rather than derives its numerical value.
consequences.conditions: a completed calibrated response/readout chain for measurement
consequences.observable: Absolute calibrated response can be g_dev-sensitive; normalized component ratios cancel g_dev and cannot determine its magnitude.

consequences.prediction: No weak-lensing deflection law or amplitude follows from A1-A3.
consequences.observable: A specified photon/effective-metric coupling is required before lensing is predicted.

consequences.prediction: Coarse graining preserves the three-component target space but does not by itself select locality, dynamics, coefficients, or a scalar observable.
consequences.observable: Kernel moments and scale separation determine finite-resolution corrections.

comparison.unique_to_three: Exactly two combinations orthogonal to one common source.
Factor 3 in normalized quadratic coherent response.

comparison.generic_n: Not defined unless representation is specified
comparison.unique_to_three: Twofold transverse degeneracy, conditional on spatial-vector identity.
Vector L/T split, not its coefficient values.

unique_predictions.claim: Two source-orthogonal microscopic combinations for a single equal common source.
unique_predictions.test: Independently excite/read component combinations; search for two dark channels.

unique_predictions.claim: Coherent quadratic response multiplicity exactly 3 rather than N or 1.
unique_predictions.test: Compare calibrated single-component and coherent susceptibilities without fitting.
unique_predictions.dependencies: A1,A2 plus common normalization and equal susceptibility

unique_predictions.claim: One longitudinal and two degenerate transverse modes.
unique_predictions.test: Directional spectroscopy/propagation measurement; test transverse degeneracy.

unique_predictions.claim: No unique scalar-lensing signature follows merely from having three components.
unique_predictions.test: Not directly testable; it is a model-identifiability constraint.
